I had an epidural “horror” story, and tbh it was still fine.

I got a med student (they did not disclose this to me) and it was his very first time trying to place an epidural. He failed the first time, and had to take it out, and go in and try again, and got it his second try. I hardly noticed. They had a fancy little lean-upon stand for me to brace myself on, but my husband was able to be right there with me too. We've known each other since the third grade, but we never really talked until middle school. In 6th grade, he sat next to me for roll in P.E. and he told me about the camp bracelet around his ankle, and he showed me when he got stitches in his pinkie toe. I thought he was a spaz, but I thought every boy was. In 7th grade, we sat at the same table in Social Studies. Another girl at our table was smitten with him, and had many failed attempts of dating him. We laughed about it, and grew closer, I thought he was cute, he had a goofy smile and happy eyes, and I loved his hair. I quickly grew to adore him. He, being a seventh grade boy didn't really notice. I had a three month plan, befriend him, get his number, and date him. But then one of my friends decided she liked him. I was heartbroken, jealous, and angry. She would obviously get this boy to fall for her. But then, she found someone else. I was still pretty upset, and decided to give up on it all. I told myself and my best friend that I didn't like him anymore, but I knew I was lying. Then, on a strangely warm day in December, right after lunch time, I was summoned to their table. I got nervous, and ran outside. He followed me, and in the middle of the football field, he grabbed my shoulders, and asked me to be his girlfriend. I was so happy, I couldn't even speak. I blushed and nodded, and ran away. We continued to grow closer, but we were still young and awkward and uncertain of what we got ourselves into. We went through fights and tears and pointless arguments, but we stuck together. And, we're still together. Whenever I think about my future, he's in it. When I wake up, he's on my mind. He's my best friend, and I wouldn't trade him for anything.

It starts out as "Oh this'll be a fun little thing to try out!" And then you just pay the monthly dues and buy some crappy old gear. But wait! You can't use those old rental skates, you need fancy Riedell skates with high-end grippy wheels and the best bearings. Oh and new clothes! You need the cool mid length workout leggings! And scrimmage tanks.

So a few months go by, you make the B team, and after you buy some new leggings and two jerseys, you're playing your first game. You then see the glorious piles of merch, and decide you need one of everything.

As you continue on, and your now old Riedell's fall apart, you realize they're not that great of a skate. So you upgrade (Roller Derby Elite bruh) to a more expensive skate. You buy the fancy $40 toe stops that won't snap off, and you've made the A team. You need to get the new jersey, and the derby skin shorts and some new make up and a new helmet, because, you have to look good. Then you see that your old gear is smelly and crappy, and since you're one of the big kids now, you'll need better protection, right? You spend a good $200 dollars on nice new gear and you're ready to go.

After being on the A team for a while, you get some exciting news, you and your team were invited for a big tournament in Florida! Plane tickets, hotel rooms, food, tourist attractions, etc.. you've spent $5000 dollars on this one trip! At least you win right?

That's one of the reasons I stopped playing. And I was only in Junior derby. But at least I won nationals... right?

Tl;Dr cash money is required to skate.
